matched_scheduler_cost.scope: End-to-end HTTP Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 workload on one AMD MI50; same clean main/candidate binaries as Linux gate, not kernel PP/TG.

protocol.cache_control: Fresh server each block. Four fixed distinct warm-up prompts plus one 1-token prime. Fresh timed prefixes share <128 tokens; cached prime matches timed prompt and must reuse256/request.
protocol.os_cache: Model bytes read/hashed before all blocks; no global cache dropping.
protocol.timing: server_load.closed_level and raw request records, one fixed run/block; no best-round selection.
protocol.monitor: Existing retained monitor at1Hz with assigned-core/cgroup counters and assigned clocks; unavailable values remain explicit; short-lived processes between snapshots may be missed.

matched_scheduler_cost.counter_witness: All candidate blocks:1024 published outputs,2056 fresh prompt rows or8 cached rows. Reuse0 fresh or2048 cached; exactly257 input/128 output tokens per request, ignore_eos recognized; no pressure pause/stall/wait deltas.
limitations: Four paired observations per cell; Student t intervals describe this fixed experiment, not every workload.
No cell discarded or replaced; all background activity retained. Activity flags do not remove observations.
New/disappeared/inaccessible processes limit process CPU accounting; raw coverage markers retained.
The observer and HTTP load client share one Python process; raw monitor-role CPU includes both, and their individual overhead is not isolated.
Matched net runtime result; individual atomic cost and C++ layout sensitivity are not isolated.
HTTP end-to-end workload throughput and latency; not kernel or per-request engine PP/TG.
matched_scheduler_cost.conclusion: No demonstrated net throughput regression in this fixed experiment. Gains/losses and wide concurrent fresh-prefix interval retained; no zero-overhead or isolated-atomic-cost claim.
